newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Texaco-led group may win Philippine contract.
newsitem.headline: Texaco-led group may win Philippine contract.

text.p: The Philippines National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Friday it will likely award a 304-megawatt power sales contract to San Pascual Cogeneration Co (SPCC) as no other company submitted a competitive bid.

"Most likely the contract will go to San Pascual since there were no competitive proposals submitted at the bidding yesterday," Cerael Donggay, Napocor negotiating committee chairman told Reuters by phone.
SPCC, a consortium composed of Texaco Inc, Caltex (Philippines) Inc and Mission Energy of the U.S., haa submitted an unsolicited proposal to build a 304-mw plant in Batangas, south of Manila.
Under the law, Napocor has to allow other interested companies to match an unsolicited proposal.
Donggay said the final round of negotiations for the contract with San Pascual should start soon. Awarding may take place within the first quarter.
Last year, four foreign companies bought bidding documents for the project -- Itochu Corp, Nissho Iwai, Salcon Power Corp of Singapore and California Energy of the United States.
The power plant which will require an estimated $400-million in investments is scheduled for commercial operation by 2001.
The San Pascual group has proposed to sell power from the Batangas plant for 1.36 per kilowatt-hour.
